title: Tata Steel shares fall 5% as investors weigh  ₹32,000 cr APL Apollo acquisition plan | Should you buy? Check key levels | Stock Market News
text:
Tata Steel shares fell over 5% on Monday, 23 November, after the steelmaker announced plans to acquire a controlling stake in structural steel tubes manufacturer APL Apollo Tubes for approximately ₹15,511 crore, alongside a mandatory open offer that could involve another ₹16,756 crore. The proposed acquisition marks a major strategic shift for Tata Steel as it looks to strengthen its presence in higher-margin, value-added steel products and expand its downstream business. Under a share purchase agreement signed with promoter group entity S Gupta Holding Pvt. Ltd., Tata Steel will acquire up to 7.38 crore equity shares of APL Apollo, representing 26.38% of its expanded voting share capital, at ₹2,100 per share. The transaction involves a total cash consideration of approximately ₹15,510.61 crore. The acquisition of the promoter stake will be completed in three phases. In the first tranche, Tata Steel is acquiring 2.77 crore shares, representing a 9.91% stake, through an on-market block deal on Monday. The remaining acquisition will take place through two off-market transfers. These comprise 3.33 crore shares, or an 11.9% stake, and another 1.28 crore shares, representing 4.57%. The transfers are expected to be completed on or before 31 March 2028, subject to regulatory approvals and fulfilment of closing conditions. Following the acquisition of the promoter stake, Tata Steel has triggered mandatory takeover provisions and announced an open offer to acquire up to 7.28 crore additional equity shares, representing 26% of APL Apollo's share capital, from public shareholders. The open offer has been priced at ₹2,301.40 per share and could entail an additional cash outlay of up to ₹16,755.66 crore if fully subscribed. If both transactions are completed in full, Tata Steel's holding in APL Apollo could rise to 52.38%, making it the company's new promoter. APL Apollo's existing promoters have proposed to move into the public shareholder category. The proposed acquisition is aimed at accelerating Tata Steel's expansion into value-added downstream products. APL Apollo brings an established portfolio of 14 brands and more than 5,000 stock-keeping units (SKUs), along with a consolidated turnover of ₹23,079 crore in FY26 across India and the UAE. Tata Steel expects its downstream integration to increase from approximately 35% to 53% following the transaction, strengthening its product portfolio and position in higher-value steel segments. The announcement comes just hours after APL Apollo disclosed its own proposed transactions with Tata Steel. APL Apollo will acquire Tata Steel's steel tubes and pipes business for up to ₹11,700 crore through a slump sale. It will also purchase the entire 100% stake in Tata Steel Colors Pvt. Ltd. for ₹16,000 crore. The proposed acquisitions are expected to be completed by 31 March 2028, subject to regulatory approvals and other customary conditions. The transactions represent a significant restructuring of the relationship between the two companies. While APL Apollo is set to take over Tata Steel's tubes and colour-coated businesses, Tata Steel is seeking majority control of APL Apollo, creating a larger platform for growth in structural steel tubes and value-added products. Tata Steel share price today opened at ₹174.80 apiece on the BSE, the stock touched an intraday low of ₹168.30 apiece, and an intraday high of ₹175.95 per share. Sudeep Shah, Head – Technical and Derivatives Research at SBI Securities, said Tata Steel has come under selling pressure following the announcement of its deal with APL Apollo Tubes, weakening from its earlier trading levels. The stock is approaching a crucial support zone of ₹164– ₹166, and a breach of this range could extend the correction towards ₹158– ₹160. On the upside, ₹173– ₹175 is likely to act as immediate resistance, followed by ₹180– ₹182. He added that the near-term technical outlook remains cautious and advised investors to wait for signs of stabilisation before taking fresh positions. Gaurav Arora, Head of Research at SAHI, said Tata Steel has been under considerable pressure and is approaching its 52-week low. He identified the ₹160– ₹162 zone as a crucial support area, warning that a breakdown below this range could intensify selling pressure. On the upside, the stock faces immediate resistance around ₹175, he said, adding that investors should closely monitor the support zone. Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only.
